newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Buy Germany's DTA dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Buy Germany's DTA dollar bond.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest trade recommendations focused on dollars, Canadian dollars, lire, sterling, marks and yen.
In Eurodollars both HSBC Markets and Tokyo-Mitsubishi suggested buying a 7.0 percent Deutsche Ausgleichsbank (DTA) bond, due September 2001.

Deutsche Ausgleichsbank has 100 percent government share ownership against 80 percent for KFW Tokyo-Mitsubishi said, and will soon enjoy greater name recognition with new issues that should tighten spreads.

Sanwa International recommended a lengthening switch in Euro-Canadian dollars, --buying a 7.25 percent Canada Special Funding bond due 2008 and selling a 6.50 percent bond due May 2001, by the same issuer.
With Canada's pending election, Sanwa said that a common feature of past elections had been a depreciating currency, so it would be a good reason to switch out of a shorter maturity.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
BUY Export-Import bank of Japan 7.0 pct 08/01 AAA
STRATEGY This switch offers a credit ratings pick-up for just a two basis point loss of yield. These are the best terms ever.
STRATEGY This move is credit neutral and offers a pick-up in yield of 10 b.p. and a two point cash take out.

STRATEGY This trade offers a credit pick-up coupled with a yield pick-up of 14 b.p. and a cash take-out of over five points. The recent widenings of the Ford 01's is unwarranted on credit fundementals and the switch terms are the best which have been available.
STRATEGY This switch offers an improvement in the credit rating of two notches and an 8 b.p. pick-up in yield.

STRATEGY The 6.25 percent Ford bond is cheap on the Ford credit curve. It is also cheap against other issues in the auto sector. The Ford rating was affirmed as stable by S&P and a Chrysler upgrade and General Motors rating revision to positive will help general sentiment towards the sector.

The Ford 6.25 percent bond is offered at 34 b.p. over its benchmark. This is signifcantly wider than the 6.125 pct December 1999 Ford bond and the 6.375 percent March 2000 Ford bond which are both "global' rather than "Euro' bonds, making them less attractive to Swiss/Benelux retail investors.

STRATEGY An intensive roadshow in the Far East to promote a 10-year Deutsche Ausgleischsbank Deutschemark bond issue, will help develop the Deutsche Ausgleischsbank name which has only two Eurodollar outstanding issues. This lack of name recognition is why the Deutsche Ausgleischsbank bonds trade much cheaper than KFW bonds. Further issues will help develop the name and allow existing spreads to tighten towards levels seen on similar Germen credits.
STRATEGY This switch gives a yield-pick up of around 84 basis points.

This switch is also in the context of the prospect of a rate hike in the U.S. in May, which may result in Canada raising its own rates once the Canadian June eletion has passed. The carrying cost between short-term Canadian dollar rates and ten-year bonds is considerably wider than in the U.S.

STRATEGY This switch shortens duration and offers around an 18 b.p. pick-up in yield. The sell side of the move is expensive against the swap at 37 b.p. through, compared to the buy side which is just 11 b.p. through.
STRATEGY The KFW on the sell side of the switches is priced at -2 b.p. against the 8.0 percent 2000 gilt and the KFW 2003 bond is priced at +16 b.p. against the 2003 gilt.
These trades overall represent a yield pick-up of 44 b.p. and gives a move to a better part of the yield curve to make capital gains given the large supply recently in the 1999-2000 area.
STRATEGY Sweden is currently trading at 11.1 b.p. through Libor compared to Finland at 5.9 b.p. through.
Although the above credit ratings show a disparity, a broad composite to equate the ratings gives both an equivelent rating of AA2.
Given a composite rating of AA2, bonds should be trading on average 6.3 b.p. through Libor, this shows Sweden to be out of line with other bonds in this area.

Sweden has been trading well due to S&P recently raffirming its long term debt rating, but a consideration for the longer term should involve EMU. Finland has a far greater chance than Sweden to make EMU in 1999, with Sweden more likely to go in on the second wave.
STRATEGY This trade should be made with expectations of curve steepening. It will deliver a yield give-up of 30 b.p. compared with a recent average of 41 b.p.
